subject: Follow-up: Data retention & backups — next steps and security questionnaire
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>

Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>

Subject: Follow-up: Data retention & backups — next steps and security questionnaire

Hi Laura / Tom,

Great speaking with you today — thanks for walking us through your retention and access requirements for the pilot. Per our conversation, I wanted to consolidate the open items and proposed next steps so we can keep procurement moving.

Quick recap of requirements you called out:
- SOC 2 status (Type II) and timeline
- GDPR/HIPAA considerations for PHI in inference traces
- Retention windows for application logs, request traces, and backups
- Ability to perform on-demand deletion for customer data and associated backup retention
- Vendor security questionnaire (VSQ) for procurement

Proposed next steps:
1) I attached a short security brief and our Retention SLA template for your review (see attachments).
2) Please share your HealthSys VSQ (I can take the first pass and Marissa can respond to technical controls).
3) Marissa (cc’d) — can you confirm our default log/backup retention and options we discussed so Laura/procurement can evaluate? I captured what we talked about below but want a precise answer to populate the VSQ.
4) Procurement: if you prefer, I can upload our answers into your DocuSign/portal once we have internal approvals.

Baseline details I promised to validate:
- Default log retention: 
  - Application request traces: 90 days (configurable)
  - Aggregated metrics: 13 months
- Backups / snapshots: retained for 180 days by default (longer term options available via add-on)
- Deletion SLA: best-effort immediate masking + data removal from live stores; formal irreversible deletion from backups as an option (requires 30–90 day processing depending on snapshot cadence)

Laura — you mentioned procurement prefers explicit SLA language around backups and restore windows. If you can share the VSQ or a short list of required clauses, I’ll prioritize those for the team.

Thanks — I’ll wait for the VSQ and loop Marissa to answer the technical specifics.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0198
Attachments: Redwood_Security_Brief.pdf (pdf), Retention_SLA_Template.docx (docx)

Hi Laura / Diego / Priyom — thanks for the ping. Below are concrete answers you can paste into the VSQ; happy to jump on a short call if you want more detail.

SOC 2:
- Current status: SOC 2 Type II in place for the core hosted API (reporting period: 2026-07-01 to 2027-06-30). Public summary and SOC cover letter are available; the full report is provided under NDA. Target: maintain Type II coverage across Dedicated/Private integrations through ongoing controls expansion.

Retention and deletion (technical specifics):
- Request traces (per-customer request logs): default retention 90 days. Configurable to 30 / 90 / 365 days via account settings or contract.
- Structured application logs (metrics and aggregated telemetry): default 13 months retention (rolling).
- Backups / snapshots: default retention 180 days. For customers requiring shorter irreversible deletion windows in backups, we offer an accelerated purge process — irreversible deletion completed within 60–90 days depending on snapshot frequency and storage provider. We can contractually cap this at 90 days.
- On-demand data deletion: requests are ingested via our deletion API/portal. Live data removal (primary stores and KV caches) is completed within 24–72 hours depending on data size. Irreversible deletion from immutable backups follows the backup purge cadence above.

PII/PHI handling:
- Redaction: we recommend customer-side redaction for PHI at ingestion as the primary control. Redwood offers optional automatic PII masking (regex-based and configurable) for request payloads and traces; however, for regulated PHI workloads we recommend using our Private deployment or Dedicated with controlled KMS.
- Encryption: data at rest is encrypted using customer-managed keys (Private/Dedicated) or Redwood-managed KMS (hosted).

Audit access and evidence:
- SOC 2: summary and cover letter attached; full SOC 2 available under NDA.
- Evidence: we can provide architecture diagrams, control narratives, and sample log retention policy documents. We can also provide an auditor liaison call if HealthSys auditors need to validate controls.

Next steps we propose:
1) Diego: pre-fill the VSQ with these answers and attach the SOC summary + architecture diagram.
2) Laura / Procurement: confirm whether you require the 90-day hard cap for backup deletion in contract language. If yes, we will supply contract wording for legal review.
3) If HealthSys wants automatic PII masking enabled for the pilot, we can demo the config and include it in the SOW.

If you want a short call to walk procurement through the answers, I’m available tomorrow 10–11am PT.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (650) 555-0123
Attachments: SOC2_Cover_Summary.pdf, Architecture_Controls_Diagram.png
